title: Piadina with prosciutto and squacquerone
intro: Romagna's classic filling: creamy fresh cheese, prosciutto and rocket.

steps.t: Heat a griddle or cast-iron pan well over medium-high heat, with no fat.
Warm one piadina at a time (store-bought is fine), turning, until it puffs and shows golden spots.
steps.label: Piadina

steps.t: Spread the cheese over half the piadina and lay on the prosciutto and a handful of rocket.
Fold into a half-moon, press and return to the pan for a few seconds per side to warm the filling. Serve at once.
steps.label: Fold

tips.t: Vegetarian version: the cheese with grilled courgettes and aubergine and a drizzle of oil.
In Romagna it comes with a glass of Sangiovese or Albana.

title: Cheddar smash burger
intro: Two thin patties smashed on a ripping-hot pan: crisp crust and melted cheese.

steps.t: Divide the beef into 8 loose 60 g balls and keep them cold. Mix mayonnaise (store-bought is fine), ketchup, mustard and chopped pickles.
Butter the cut buns and toast them cut side down in a pan until golden.
steps.label: Buns

steps.t: Heat a cast-iron pan until smoking. Add 2 balls, cover with baking paper and smash to 5 mm with a spatula. Salt and pepper.
Cook without moving until the edges are deep brown and crisp.
steps.label: Crust

steps.t: Scrape them up, flip, put cheese on half the patties and cook until the meat is cooked through and the cheese melts.
steps.label: Cheese

steps.t: Build: sauce, 2 stacked patties, paper-thin onion and pickles. Repeat with the remaining balls.

tips.t: Cold meat, ripping-hot pan: smash once, within the first 10 seconds, and never again.
Put thin-sliced onion on the ball before smashing so it caramelizes into the meat (Oklahoma style).

title: Arancini with ragù
intro: Saffron rice balls with a heart of meat ragù, peas and caciocavallo, fried golden.

steps.t: Bring the stock (store-bought is fine) to a boil with the saffron, add the rice and cook, stirring now and then, until absorbed and al dente.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Off the heat, beat in butter and grated cheese, spread the rice on a tray, cover with film and let it cool completely.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the ragù (homemade or store-bought) with the peas until nice and thick, then let it cool.
steps.label: Ragù

steps.t: With wet hands take about 120 g of rice, make a hollow, add a spoonful of ragù and a few cubes of cheese and close into a ball.
Whisk flour and water into a smooth batter, dip the arancini in it and roll them in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry 2 or 3 at a time until deep golden. Drain on paper.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Spray the arancini with oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, turning halfway.

oven.t: Oil the arancini, set them on a lined tray and bake at 220 °C fan for 25 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Let them rest a few minutes before serving: the middle is scorching.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: The rice must be completely cold, even made the day before; warm rice won't hold its shape.
In Palermo they also make them 'al burro': ham, mozzarella and béchamel instead of ragù.

title: Crispy tofu bao
intro: Pillowy steamed buns with crispy hoisin-glazed tofu and fresh vegetables.

steps.t: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add water and oil and knead for 8 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Cover and leave to rise somewhere warm until doubled.
steps.label: First rise

steps.t: Meanwhile, press the tofu between two towels, cut into 12 slices 1 cm thick and toss in cornstarch with a pinch of salt.
Mix hoisin, soy sauce and vinegar. Cut cucumber and carrot into thin sticks and chop the peanuts.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, roll into 3 mm ovals, brush the tops with oil and fold in half. Set each on a square of baking paper.
Cover and let them rise again.
steps.label: Second rise

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the tofu in the oil, 3 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Turn off the heat and toss it in half the sauce.
steps.label: Tofu

airfryer.t: Meanwhile, oil the tofu and air-fry at 200 °C for 12 minutes, turning halfway. Then toss it in half the sauce.

steps.t: Steam the bao, covered, in a bamboo steamer over simmering water. Turn off and leave the lid on for 2 minutes before opening.
steps.label: Steam

steps.t: Open the buns, brush with the remaining sauce and fill with tofu, vegetables, peanuts and cilantro.

tips.t: Steamed bao freeze well: re-steam them straight from frozen for 6 minutes.
The classic Taiwanese gua bao uses braised pork belly, pickled mustard greens and sweet peanuts.

title: Lemongrass chicken banh mi
intro: Vietnam's sandwich: crusty baguette, caramelized chicken and quick-pickled veg.

steps.t: Cut carrots and daikon into matchsticks and put them in a bowl with vinegar, water, 2 tbsp sugar and salt. Leave them to pickle.
steps.label: Pickles

steps.t: Meanwhile, finely chop the tender part of the lemongrass and the garlic, mix with fish sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp oil and marinate the sliced chicken.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Cook the chicken in a hot pan with the remaining oil, 4 minutes per side, until caramelized and cooked through with no pink.
steps.label: Chicken

grill.t: Cook the chicken on a very hot grill pan, 5 minutes per side, until charred, caramelized and cooked through with no pink.

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the baguettes in the oven at 200 °C until the crust is crisp again.
steps.label: Bread

steps.t: Thinly slice cucumber and chilli and drain the pickles.
Split the baguettes, spread with mayonnaise (store-bought is fine) and fill with chicken, pickles, cucumber, cilantro and chilli.

tips.t: Pull out some of the crumb from the baguette: more room for filling and the bread stays crisp.
Vegan version: tofu marinated in soy instead of chicken and fish sauce, plus vegan mayo.

title: Pane e panelle
intro: Palermo street food: hot chickpea-flour fritters stuffed into a sesame roll.

steps.t: In a saucepan, whisk the chickpea flour into the cold water with the salt until there are no lumps.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until very thick and pulling away from the sides, like polenta.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Stir in parsley and pepper and quickly spread the mixture 5 mm thick on an oiled surface or tray, levelling with a wet spatula.
Let it cool until firm enough to cut cleanly.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Cut into 5×7 cm rectangles and fry in oil at 180 °C until golden and puffed. Drain on paper.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Cut into rectangles, brush lightly with oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 12 minutes, turning halfway.

oven.t: Cut into rectangles, oil them and bake on a lined tray at 220 °C for 20 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Stuff the rolls with the hot panelle, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Eat straight away.

tips.t: In Palermo the full version is 'pane, panelle e crocchè': add fried potato croquettes.
The cut, uncooked panelle freeze well: fry them straight from frozen.
